units.spec_id: lessons.md §1 — dedicated search worker bypasses the global worker lifecycle (shutdown crash)
units.deviation: The old app introduced a second QThread lane and could crash on shutdown. The new app has no QThread or per-feature worker lane: one Tauri async runtime plus RAII guards own every registration. Residual gap: no explicit shutdown/quit test was added where the old lesson called one mandatory.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\PHASE16_11_3_SEARCH_GLOBAL_WORKER_STABILITY_FIX_REPORT.md:9-16 (a dedicated `search_thread`/`search_worker` diverged from `_run_worker()`, the GUI crashed after a search, and the fix routed search back through the one worker while ignoring stale results) and :22-25 (cleanup deferred until the original thread fully finished). New side: src-tauri/src/state.rs:418-437 lets `end_install` clear the slot only when `Arc::ptr_eq` matches the flag that run registered, so a late finish cannot cancel the next run; :573-596 `InstallGuard::drop` calls `end_install` on every exit path, and :598-620 does the same for transfers; core/src/watcher.rs:178-182 joins the single watcher thread on Drop. The bypassable second lane is gone by construction; state.rs:1086-1091 asserts the slot is empty after the run.

units.spec_id: lessons.md §2 — stale result from a cancelled task corrupts the new result
units.deviation: The old generation token is re-implemented as `RequestGate`; the new side additionally gates resets that send no request (cache hit, provider switch), a case the old report did not cover.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\docs\release\PHASE16_11_7_IMMEDIATE_SEARCH_INTERRUPT_FIX_REPORT.md:39-56: cancel invalidated the current generation and stale results/errors were discarded by token, because the old worker could keep running after interruption. New side: src/app/browse/paging.ts:40-62 implements `next()`, `isCurrent()` and `invalidate()`, with :35-38 naming F-166 and the reason (Tauri `invoke()` has no AbortSignal); src/app/browse/paging.test.ts:66-92 proves `spec_f166_a_superseded_request_never_renders` (older generation is not current) and `spec_f166_a_cache_hit_or_a_reset_invalidates_the_in_flight_response` (a reset with no request still closes the window); src/app/pages/BrowsePage.tsx:111-113,164-166,240-246 call it on provider switch and on cache hits.

units.spec_id: lessons.md §3 — cancellation reported as an empty success
units.deviation: The old `finished(path, 0)` fake success is replaced by a typed `Cancelled` code that reaches both the Tauri Channel and the promise; no empty-Ok path remains for a user cancel.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\PHASE16_19_41_IMPORT_CANCEL_HARDENING_REPORT.md:5-12 (cancel looked like a successful empty import and `.mrpack` preview had no terminal signal) and :27-59 (`cancelled = Signal(str)` plus a terminal cancel for scan, import, preview and export). New side: src-tauri/src/dto.rs:92-96 defines `ErrorCode::Cancelled` as 'not a failure at all', with the `.part` kept for resume; src-tauri/src/commands.rs:1080-1091 states the cancel is reported through `install.phase.cancelled` and the promise. src-tauri/src/commands/channel_tests.rs:553-623 (`spec_f036_a_cancel_during_the_resolve_phase_is_cancelled`) asserts the promise rejects with `ErrorCode::Cancelled`, no file is downloaded, and history stores `Cancelled` rather than `Failed`; src-tauri/src/commands/backup_tests.rs:384-409 applies the same rule to backup.

units.spec_id: lessons.md §4 (4.1/4.2/4.3) — scan prune, PRESENT vs ELIGIBLE data-deletion bug, missing file veto
units.deviation: The §4.2 bug did NOT return. The new code computes PRESENT (disk scan) and ELIGIBLE (lock entries a file satisfies) as two separate sets, and `spec_f131_present_but_ineligible_entry_is_not_a_prune_candidate` pins the exact old regression: an incompatibility verdict is not absence.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\PHASE16_18_3_SAVED_MODS_MISSING_FILE_PRUNE_FIX_REPORT.md:12-18: the old sync-prune received only `dialog.import_matches()` (the import-compatible subset), so a project physically present but skipped for incompatibility was counted missing and pruned; the fix added `present_project_ids()`. New side: core/src/updates/target.rs:7-18 states 'Two sets, never one' and names the §4.2 data deletion: PRESENT is the disk scan, ELIGIBLE is what the lock records; :316-322 computes `present_entries` from `scan_mods_recursive` and separately calls `candidates_for`, and :417-418 reports `present_files: facts.len()` against `eligible_files` counted from lock entries. core/src/updates/prune.rs:269-283 makes a candidate only when `!entry_is_present(entry, facts)`, and :183-189 re-checks presence at execute time, so incompatibility never deletes a record. Proof: core/src/updates/target_tests.rs:800-828 `spec_f131_present_but_ineligible_entry_is_not_a_prune_candidate` makes alpha incompatible with the target yet on disk and asserts `alpha.file_present`, `plan.prune_candidates.is_empty()` and `eligible_files == 1`; :832-855 `spec_f131_present_and_eligible_are_counted_as_two_sets` asserts present_files=2 and eligible_files=1. The §4.1 sibling is core/src/updates/prune_tests.rs:74-94 `spec_f130_dry_run_lists_only_lock_entries_with_no_file` (bytes unchanged), and §4.3 is :125-141 `spec_f130_prune_keeps_an_entry_whose_file_reappeared` (presence vetoes removal at execute).

units.spec_id: lessons.md §5 — created profile never becomes the active scan/import context
units.deviation: There is no implicit active-profile context in the new IPC: the target is an explicit id or root in every command, and compatibility filtering moved into the read-only validator rather than a dialog selection state.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\PHASE16_13_PROFILE_INSTANCE_SCAN_IMPORT_METADATA_FIX_REPORT.md:11-16 (the new profile was selected but not activated, so Link Instance / Scan Installed acted on another context and imported versions that did not match the target) and :37-44 (the old fix filtered incompatible projects in the import dialog). New side: src-tauri/src/commands.rs:441-447 declares `validate_instance(state, instance_id: String)`; :451-474 trims and rejects an empty id as `invalid_input`, resolves it with `db::instances::get`, and passes that row — not a webview-chosen folder — to `validate_instance`, with :438-440 stating 'the row is the input, not the folder'. The compatibility judgement is exercised in core/src/instances/tests.rs:373-420 `spec_f097_compatibility_needs_positive_metadata` and :547-632 where recorded ranges are judged against the instance target.

units.spec_id: lessons.md §6 — a diagnostic that checks everything slows the common-target path
units.deviation: The per-run cache is kept, but the old per-worker diagnostics log is dropped by the recorded F-059 decision, so only cache behaviour — not the hit/miss log — is ported.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\PHASE16_19_17_COMMON_TARGET_PERFORMANCE_CACHE_REPORT.md:31-39 (resolver verification was restricted to strict-common candidates and raw metadata explained the rest, which made the suggestion faster without changing the answer) and D:\latest_project\docs\release\PHASE16_19_34_RESOLVER_RUN_CACHE_DIAGNOSTICS.md:29-31 (cache scoped to one run/worker, never global, so no stale cross-run answers). New side: core/src/resolver/cache.rs:1-5 says the cache is owned by one resolve run and dropped with it and that diagnostics are dropped per F-059; :69-85 defines `RunCache::new(enabled)` and every read/write returns early when disabled. core/src/updates/target.rs:278,282 construct it per planner call, and core/src/updates/target_tests.rs:940-979 `spec_f132_planner_reads_a_seeded_run_cache` seeds both metadata keys and proves the plan is built without a provider refetch. docs/spec/features.md:109 records F-059 diagnostics as Drop, so the absent log is a decision, not a regression.

units.spec_id: lessons.md §7 — packaging-stage failures read as general architecture patterns
units.deviation: The PowerShell/WSL build scripts themselves are replaced by the Tauri bundler (recorded in ws3); the architectural lessons survive as typed data instead of interpolated command strings, and the disk-preflight lesson is enforced before any HTTP request.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\PHASE13_0_1_RC_CHECK_POWERSHELL_INTERPOLATION_FIX_REPORT.md:9-13 (a colon after `$Name` inside a double-quoted string broke the RC script), D:\latest_project\PHASE14_0_3_WSLPATH_EXEC_FIX_REPORT.md:16-28 (`D:\Downloads\...` lost its backslashes before `wslpath`), and D:\latest_project\PHASE12_6_5_INSTALLER_QA_DISK_SPACE_PREFLIGHT_REPORT.md:22-37 (the same low-disk failure recurred at different build stages until free-space preflight was added). New side: core/src/downloader/client.rs:268-276 probes free space when `expected_size` is known and returns `DownloadError::NoSpace` before any request; :687-697 walks to the nearest existing ancestor so a not-yet-created destination still probes the right volume; core/src/downloader/client.rs:1185-1200 `spec_f023_disk_preflight_blocks` injects a 1-byte probe against a 1,000,000-byte download and asserts zero requests reached wiremock. Error identity is typed at src-tauri/src/commands/tests.rs:38-63 (NotFound maps to NotFound, other IO causes to Io, newer schema to its own code) rather than parsed out of a message.

units.spec_id: lessons.md §8 — painful areas: licensing, Linux packaging, Windows long paths, 13k-line main window
units.deviation: The licensing/activation and PyInstaller/Inno/AppImage costs are retired by explicit user decisions (F-175, F-176, F-177, F-178) rather than reimplemented; the monolith cost is paid down by keeping core free of Tauri and leaving commands.rs as IPC glue only.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\app\licensing.py:18-32 (license/environment/public-key constants and two signature algorithms — measured 420 lines at HEAD 4f71f18) and D:\latest_project\PROJECT_MAP.md (measured 1003 lines); the old `app/ui/main_window.py` measures 14271 lines. New side: docs/spec/features.md:282-286 records F-175 licensing, F-176 PyInstaller/Inno/AppImage, F-177 public/private modes and F-178 diagnostics templates as Drop, with decision-sheet.md:9 confirming the final licensing decision; src-tauri/src/commands.rs is 1618 lines and core/src/lib.rs 97 lines by direct measurement, and AGENTS.md §5.1 forbids any Tauri dependency in core. This is a recorded decision, not an accidental omission, so no old cost silently returned.

units.spec_id: lessons.md §9 — checklist L-1..L-13, especially L-10 (broad assertRaises hides the failing call)
units.deviation: The old broad `assertRaises(OSError)` is replaced by typed ErrorCode assertions that name the exact failure class. Other checklist items are carried by the spec-named tests cited earlier: L-2/L-5 by `spec_f131_*` and `spec_f130_dry_run_*`, L-3 by `spec_f036_*`, L-8 by serde-based DTOs.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\tests\qa\test_database_migrations.py:592-605: `with self.assertRaises(OSError)` wraps `_publish_backup` while an OSError is injected into `_sync_directory`, so any unrelated OSError would pass; docs/spec/tests-to-port.md:39-49 names this exact test and recommends narrowing the assertion to the failing call. New side: src-tauri/src/commands/tests.rs:8-64 `spec_f104_registry_errors_map_to_codes` asserts per-case codes, distinguishing `ErrorKind::NotFound` -> NotFound from `Error::other("not a folder")` -> InvalidInput and `PermissionDenied` -> Io at :38-63, instead of accepting any IO error. core/src/updates/prune.rs:3-10 makes the dry run mandatory and refuses a confirm that was never planned, and core/src/updates/prune_tests.rs:163-178 `spec_f130_execute_refuses_a_record_the_dry_run_never_showed` asserts `PruneError::LockChanged` with zero removals.

units.spec_id: lessons.md §10 — mark what is unverified instead of guessing
units.deviation: The new spec set keeps the old epistemic rule: values not observed in the live capture or not exercised by a test are labelled instead of asserted. The old study's deferred formats are now recorded as decisions rather than left open.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\docs\release\PHASE18_23_IMPORT_FORMAT_EXPANSION_STUDY.md:25-28 (CurseForge zip and Packwiz marked Defer with 'feasibility document first', raw unknown zip 'Avoid for now') — a study, not a fix, which is why lessons.md:198 declines to treat it as a lesson. New side: docs/spec/fixtures.md:560-566 explicitly lists `releaseType`, `fileStatus`, the absent 429/header observation and the 1/51 `allowModDistribution` sample as غير مُتحقَّق, and docs/spec/tests-to-port.md:256,264-267 states the 850/33-file figures are derived from cache and source rather than a test run; docs/spec/lessons.md:191-201 itself closes with the same rule. Nothing here is promoted to a verified claim on assumption.

units.deviation: The old real `ThreadingHTTPServer` cases are re-expressed with wiremock and finer spec-named tests. No external network and no real sleeps remain, which removes the old flakiness class.
units.evidence: Read the old test file: `test_download_commits_only_verified_artifact` at :266, `test_download_resumes_partial_file_with_range_request` at :275, `test_verification_failure_never_commits_and_discards_invalid_partial` at :606 and `test_disk_preflight_blocks_download_before_request` at :626; tests-to-port.md:67-80 lists this group and recommends wiremock. New side: core/src/downloader/client.rs:951 `spec_f021_download_commits_verified`, :977 `spec_f034_hash_mismatch_deletes_part`, :1042 `spec_f026_resume_appends_on_206`, :1061 `spec_f026_restart_when_server_ignores_range`, :1025 `spec_f027_no_retry_on_404`, :1185-1200 `spec_f023_disk_preflight_blocks` (asserts zero requests on refusal) and :1204 `spec_f030_html_rejected_deletes_part`; the terminal-event rule is core/src/downloader/batch_tests.rs:608 `spec_f020_a_cancelled_batch_still_emits_a_terminal_event`.
